_comment: S3 Cross-Region Replication configuration — attaches to
agrisync-raw-ap-south-1 (SOURCE), replicating to
agrisync-raw-backup-ap-south-2 (DESTINATION, ap-south-2 / Hyderabad).
spec: FINAL_SERVER_AUTHORITATIVE_EXECUTION_PLAN (raw-bucket-backup-recovery)
AUTHORED, NOT APPLIED.
<ACCOUNT_ID> and the role ARN below must be filled in before apply —
apply-replication.sh does this substitution; do not hand-edit and apply
this file directly with a placeholder still in it.
DeleteMarkerReplication is explicitly DISABLED. A delete marker on the
source (soft-delete) is NOT copied to the destination — this is what
makes the destination a genuine backup rather than a mirror that
faithfully reproduces every mistake made on the source, including the
exact class of event this whole system was built in response to.
Filter is empty (whole-bucket) — every prefix replicates, not just
raw/. The bucket also carries deploy-staging traffic (see the runbook's
root-cause section) which does not need backing up, but there is no
reliable way to distinguish 'deploy staging, safe to skip' from 'real
evidence' by prefix alone without trusting deploy tooling to keep using
a stable, documented prefix — which it does not do today (undocumented,
ad-hoc). Replicating everything costs pennies more; replicating too
little risks missing real evidence because of a naming assumption. The
runbook's recommended follow-up (retire the raw-bucket-as-deploy-staging
pattern) removes this cost entirely rather than trying to filter around it.
APPLY (founder only, via apply-replication.sh):
aws s3api put-bucket-replication --bucket agrisync-raw-ap-south-1 --replication-configuration file://<rendered> --region ap-south-1
